verdict.root_cause: cartservice stopped serving at 11:41:33 and never returned. Its last log line is an orderly framework shutdown with no preceding error, and a cartservice image-reference update to the v1.2.1-cartservice-hotfix.2 tag was applied by platform-automation at 11:41:34 with no revert recorded and no startup lines afterwards [tr_3bb52a71e4b1, tr_cbac745c2d45]. Checkout failures three minutes later all abort on checkoutservice's client span for CartService/GetCart, error-marked, with no cartservice server span and no Redis child, in 3-6ms fast-fail traces [tr_98e1e1ba774d]. checkoutservice itself is clean: no post-onset changes, error ratio at or below baseline, no error logs, still accepting traffic but never reaching payment/email/queue steps [tr_94897908dac8, tr_aa5d047bd3fb, tr_22bac06b1a5c]. The mechanism is that the artifact now referenced for cartservice is not running and serving requests.
verdict.reasoning: Timing ties the image update at 11:41:34 to cartservice's final log line one second earlier, with no restart in the following 5.5 minutes [tr_cbac745c2d45, tr_3bb52a71e4b1]. The caller-side failure shape confirms absence rather than error or slowness: the error sits on checkoutservice's GetCart client span with no server-side or cache child, and traces fast-fail in 3-6ms instead of timing out [tr_98e1e1ba774d]. checkoutservice is exonerated as origin by its unchanged error ratio, absent error logs, continued traffic ingestion, and lack of any post-cart spans [tr_aa5d047bd3fb, tr_22bac06b1a5c, tr_94897908dac8]. Rival cartservice stories are excluded by their own specialists: the REDIS_ADDR repoint and 300ms traffic-shaping container were reverted ~3h before onset [tr_cbac745c2d45]; crash, OOM and restart-loop are inconsistent with one clean shutdown and no stack trace [tr_3bb52a71e4b1]; Redis slowdown is excluded since no backend span exists at all [tr_98e1e1ba774d]. This is bad_deploy because what is wrong now is which artifact is (not) running, not a wrong config value, a wait, or an exhausted resource; rollback to the prior cartservice image is the fix, as in every earlier cycle of this tag.
open_questions: No pod-level data was gathered (image pull events, exit codes, restart counts, readiness), so whether hotfix.2 failed to pull, crash-looped before logging, or was never scheduled is unsettled.
The same tag was applied and reverted at least four times earlier in the window with no reported impact [tr_cbac745c2d45]; why this application caused an incident is unexplained.

cartservice call metrics are empty in both incident and baseline windows, so there is no independent metric confirmation of the outage timing [tr_1e644881c6a7]; and the pre-onset change window for checkoutservice and other dependencies was never queried [tr_94897908dac8].

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice pods terminated at 11:41 could not be rescheduled due to cluster capacity limits, leaving the endpoint empty.
alternatives.why_not: No evidence of any resource constraint was collected; the shutdown was orderly with no OOM or kill signature [tr_3bb52a71e4b1], and an image change one second earlier is a far more direct explanation [tr_cbac745c2d45].

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix.2 image carries a wrong configuration value (e.g. bad cache address or port) so the new cartservice starts but cannot serve.
alternatives.why_not: No cartservice startup or error lines appear after the shutdown, so there is no evidence a new instance ran and misconfigured itself; the last recorded REDIS_ADDR edit was reverted ~2.8h before onset [tr_3bb52a71e4b1, tr_cbac745c2d45].

proposal.expected_effect: Loki {service="cart-service"} resumes startup lines then GetCartAsync traffic, ending the silence since 11:41:33; checkoutservice's CartService/GetCart client span loses its error mark and regains a cartservice server child plus Redis HGET, with traces returning from ~5 spans/3-6ms to the intact ~36-48 span/~24ms shape; checkoutservice logs resume payment, email and queue-write lines per order. Cartservice metrics are empty in both windows and will confirm nothing.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if no cartservice startup lines appear within 5 minutes (a pull failure or pre-log crash, which the ungathered pod-level data cannot presently exclude and this action would not fix), or if the service starts but GetCart client spans stay error-marked with no server child. The change log records the prior value as 'None', so verify a concrete earlier tag exists before executing.
proposal.risk: If hotfix.2 was the intended artifact and the 11:41:33 shutdown came from the automation cycle, this pins a stale build and platform-automation may re-apply the tag on its ~5-hourly cadence, reproducing the outage. If no usable prior reference exists, the recreate leaves cartservice down longer. It also destroys the current container, losing exit code and image-pull evidence that would settle why hotfix.2 never started.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only. checkoutservice (its named caller) and through it frontend and loadgenerator see connection resets during the recreate, on a dependency already not serving.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical simultaneous alerts on checkout and frontend plus the load generator indicate user-facing failure, not a quiet system. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not favor a specific fault class.
